transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-09-14 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes | Attendees: Lena Park, Marco Díaz, Priya Narayanan (Redwood); Aisha Patel, Ben Yu, Darren Cole, Sofia Ramos (Thalassa)

[00:00] Lena Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time on a tuesday afternoon. i'm lena from redwood, i'm the account lead on this.
[00:07] Aisha Patel: hi lena, thanks, excited to get into this.
[00:09] Ben Yu: hey all.
[00:11] Marco Díaz: hey team, marco here, i will mostly run the demo and the performance bits.
[00:15] Sofia Ramos: morning — or afternoon — yeah, good to be here.
[00:18] Lena Park: quick agenda: we'll do a short context/qual — what you want to achieve with relevance — then i'll hand to marco for the hosted embeddings + rerank flow demo via the api and console optimize suggestions, then q&a and next steps. sound good?
[00:31] Aisha Patel: yep that works. for context: thalassa is building an internal docs search aimed at engineering and customer success; currently using a keyword system and an off-the-shelf vector db — we want better reranking and less manual feature engineering. primary metrics are p50 relevance click-through increase, and p95 latency under 170ms for interactive queries. cost per query ideally < $0.02, but flex.
[00:56] Lena Park: great, thanks for the goals. quick question on volume — what qps should we plan for in the pilot?
[01:02] Darren Cole: pilot target is small, like 2-5 qps, but full swing could be 200 qps later. for pilot we just need to validate accuracy and tail latency. also security: all data must remain private; we'd prefer hosted but need SOC2 docs and KMS integration details.
[01:17] Marco Díaz: noted. we'll show how hosted api keeps docs private (no long-term retention unless you opt in) and KMS support for encryption at rest.
[01:25] Marco Díaz: okay demo start — i'm going to share my screen, ping me if visuals don't show.
[01:31] [screen share noise]
[01:33] Marco Díaz: first, the typical embeddings + rerank flow: ingest -> embed via /v1/embeddings -> store vectors in your vector store -> at query time we do a lightweight nearest-neighbor retrieval -> call redwood's rerank endpoint which accepts the query, candidate doc ids, and returns a score/ordering. the rerank model can run in the hosted api tier with microsecond-scale scoring that is optimized for batching.
[02:05] Ben Yu: quick q — are you doing the rerank scoring on the vectors or do you send raw text? i.e., do you re-embed candidate doc passages?
[02:12] Marco Díaz: good question. our hosted reranker can accept either precomputed embeddings or raw passages. for performance we usually send the candidate ids + a small text snippet for context; if you already have embeddings stored we can accept them and skip re-embedding. note: re-embedding at rerank time helps small prompt-context models but costs more.
[02:32] [00:02 audio glitch — "re-embedding" becomes "re-bridging"]
[02:35] Aisha Patel: and the console — can we see suggestions for batching / quantization?
[02:39] Marco Díaz: yep, switch to the console view — the Optimize tab surfaces batching recommendations, cache policies (prefix caching), and quantization suggestions based on your workload histogram. here's an example: for short queries (tokens < 64) we recommend batch size 8 with continuous batching and prefix cache enabled; estimates show ~35% token cost reduction.
[03:04] Sofia Ramos: those are auto suggestions or do they require manual tuning?
[03:08] Marco Díaz: auto suggestions are a starting point — you can accept them globally or per-model route. also you can pin quantization profiles for a given rollout.
[03:16] Ben Yu: can i run evals on my testset in the console? like run our sample queries and get nDCG / MRR metrics?
[03:22] Marco Díaz: yes, the console supports dataset-driven evals — you upload a set, run a job and it will compute relevance metrics and show diffs between model versions or reranker configs. it's helpful to avoid regressions during rollouts.
[03:34] Darren Cole: about retention — you said no long-term retention by default, but what about logs for debugging?
[03:40] Priya Narayanan: by default we store request-level logs for a short window (configurable retention), and we can turn on/off transcript capture. for enterprise/private you can ship logs to your s3 or use the private control plane. we also support audit logs for user actions.
[03:56] Aisha Patel: SOC2 — do you have SOC2 and iso certs?
[03:59] Lena Park: yes we are SOC2 Type II, and we have ISO attestation materials; i'll send the security pack. we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations in Private, and hosted can be configured for crypto-key separation too.
[04:15] Ben Yu: okay moving back to the rerank performance — can you show a sample latency run?
[04:19] Marco Díaz: sure — here's a quick curl to the embeddings endpoint, then the rerank call. i'll run a synthetic 1k query bench now using a small subset of thalassa-like docs (note: i'm using a cached prefix so numbers are optimistic).
[04:33] [keystrokes]
[04:35] Marco Díaz: results — p50 is ~45ms, p95 around 160ms for rerank-only when we pass precomputed embeddings and use batch size 8. end-to-end from query to final ordering including a nearest-neighbor fetch in your vector DB was ~220ms in this synthetic run, since the vector store fetch is the variability point.
[04:58] Ben Yu: 220ms end-to-end — can we get that under 170ms?
[05:02] Marco Díaz: likely yes with a few levers: colocate vector store and redwood regionally to remove network hop, enable prefix/KV caching for common queries, and tune batch sizes. the console Optimize suggestion flagged a 30% improvement if you enable prefix cache and move to batch size 12 for your short query distribution.
[05:22] Aisha Patel: cost — what's typical per-query with this setup?
[05:26] Lena Park: depends on tokens and reranker model size. for short queries with precomputed embeddings and a lightweight reranker, customers we work with see $0.006–$0.02/query at scale; we'll send more precise breakdowns in the pricing doc.
[05:38] Darren Cole: any hidden egress or data scanning costs?
[05:41] Priya Narayanan: egress depends on your vector store location and your cloud; we surface token-level cost in the console and you can set per-route quotas and alerts.
[05:53] Sofia Ramos: is there a way to do canary rollouts for reranker changes? we want to test new configs on a small percent of traffic.
[05:59] Marco Díaz: yes — rollout policies support canary, A/B, and auto-fallback. you can pin a rollout to a model version and route percent traffic to it. console shows live metrics for both variants so you can compare CTR and latency.
[06:12] [short pause]
[06:15] Aisha Patel: from a security POV, if we go hosted, we need to ensure PII is not used to train models and that no customer content is stored beyond retention. can you confirm?
[06:24] Lena Park: yes — hosted does not use customer payloads to improve models by default. data use policies are laid out in the SOW; we can add contractual clauses. we'll include the exact language in the packet i send.
[06:37] Ben Yu: small nit — any weird tokenization edge cases with our code snippets? e.g., long stack traces or base64 blobs?
[06:45] Marco Díaz: stack traces can be truncated or chunked; we recommend pre-processing to split long passages. also the embeddings endpoint supports a chunker helper in our sdk to create overlapping passages for better locality.
[06:59] Aisha Patel: alright, let's talk pilot scope — what would a quick success criteria look like for thalassa?
[07:05] Lena Park: proposed pilot: 10k docs ingest, 1k query test set, run embeddings + rerank w/ two config variants (baseline and redwood-optimized), run console evals for nDCG/MRR, and do a 7-day smoke to measure p95 latency and user impact. if accuracy and latency meet your thresholds, we move to a reserved capacity discuss.
[07:29] Sofia Ramos: sounds reasonable. timeline?
[07:32] Lena Park: if you can provide docs by 2027-09-16 we'll run a benchmark and share results by 2027-09-21. pilot kickoff could be end of September.
[07:42] Ben Yu: i'll upload the sample docs, but need to check anonymization.
[07:46] Darren Cole: i'll confirm network egress constraints and whether we need VPC peering or private endpoint.
[07:50] Marco Díaz: if you need private connectivity we can do private endpoints or recommend our Private deployment — for pilot hosted usually suffices with strict retention and KMS.
[07:59] [audio overlap, "private endpoints" / "pilot hosted"]
[08:03] Aisha Patel: one more technical — reranker model training: are you using a static reranker or do you do online learning?
[08:09] Marco Díaz: hosted reranker is a pre-trained neural model we fine-tune per-customer during onboarding if you want, but we don't do continuous ingestion-based retraining without customer opt-in. you can provide labels and we'll do a controlled re-tune.
[08:23] Ben Yu: can we host the reranker in our private deployment later?
[08:27] Lena Park: yes, you can move reranker to Dedicated or Private and keep the same api surface. that's one of our differentiators — same routes, different infra.
[08:35] Sofia Ramos: ok good.
[08:37] Marco Díaz: quick note on observability — console gives token-level cost, per-request traces, and tracing hooks for your app to attach request ids. you can also export traces to jaeger/OTel.
[08:50] Ben Yu: great.
[08:53] Lena Park: any other questions?
[08:55] Aisha Patel: i think that's most of it. can you re-iterate what you'll send after the call?
[08:59] Lena Park: sure — i'll send: 1) pricing + hosted vs dedicated pilot options, 2) SOC2/security packet and KMS integration notes, 3) a short pilot SOW template, 4) a link to the benchmark spreadsheet and the console walk-through recording.
[09:18] Marco Díaz: i'll also share the synthetic bench logs and the curl snippets i used, and i'll run the 1k-query bench on thalassa sample once ben uploads it.
[09:28] Aisha Patel: perfect. thanks everyone.
[09:30] Lena Park: thanks all — we'll follow up with dates.
[09:33] [meeting ends]

Notes: occasional transcription errors — e.g., "re-bridging" for re-embedding; timestamps approximated. Shared artifacts referenced: https://redwood.example.com/pilot/thalassa-deck (demo deck), https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/thalassa-2027-09 (bench spreadsheet).
